title: Jeff Kilburg
summary: Jeff Kilburg is the Founder, CEO, and CIO of KKM Financial, an asset management company in Chicago, IL. KKM Financial offers various services including outsourced CIO services, model portfolios, and market commentary globally. Kilburg also serves as a portfolio manager for the Essential 40 Stock ETF (ESN) and contributes market insights and options trading strategies to CNBC.

title: Walmart Canada makes online shopping easier
summary: Walmart Canada has partnered with 7-Eleven Canada Inc. to expand its Grab & Go locker network in the greater Toronto area, allowing customers to pick up online orders for free 24/7. This initiative aims to make online shopping more convenient by leveraging 7-Eleven's presence in customers' daily routines. The partnership begins with a six-month pilot to evaluate customer response and usage.

title: Vimeo steps up original content efforts with ‘The Outs,’ ‘Darby’ and ‘Rolodex’
summary: Vimeo is significantly increasing its original programming with a new slate of three shows: a second season of the gay comedy "The Outs," a short film "Darby Forever" starring Aidy Bryant, and "Rolodex of Hate Comedy Special" with Bianca Del Rio. The company, a division of IAC, aims to attract creators with favorable revenue splits and audiences with unique, lower-budget content, building on the success of its earlier viral hit "High Maintenance." These new offerings will be available for a fee on Vimeo's on-demand platform.

title: Netflix Raising US Price For Most Popular Video Plan By $1
summary: Netflix is increasing the price of its most popular internet video plan by $1 for new customers in the U.S., Canada, and some Latin American countries, raising it to $10 per month. This move is to help cover escalating costs for original programming and content acquisition, as the company faces increasing competition. Existing subscribers will be insulated from this price hike, a strategy implemented after a significant customer backlash from a previous price increase.

title: Cert. Sought in Amazon Background Check Class Action Lawsuit
summary: A class action lawsuit against Amazon and staffing company SMX, alleging violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) for denying employment based on undisclosed background checks, is seeking class certification. The lead plaintiff, Gregory Williams, was denied employment at an Amazon warehouse due to an incorrect, undisclosed background check and his attorneys are pursuing certification for two nationwide classes to prevent individual settlement offers from derailing the case. Hundreds of thousands of applicants could be affected due to SMX's standardized procedures and Amazon's high volume hiring, especially during holidays.

title: Four Ohio CEOs rank among the world's 100 best-performing CEOs, Harvard Business Review says
summary: Four Ohio CEOs, including Leslie Wexner of L Brands and Chris Connor of Sherwin-Williams, have been named among the world's 100 best-performing CEOs by Harvard Business Review. The ranking considers both financial performance and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors. This marks a shift from previous rankings that solely focused on stock market numbers, allowing for a more comprehensive evaluation of leadership.

title: Workhorse drone company tests package deliveries in Ohio
summary: Workhorse Group Inc. and the University of Cincinnati are testing drone package deliveries in Ohio using a drone named HorseFly that launches from electric delivery trucks. The Federal Aviation Administration granted a two-year certificate for testing at the Wilmington Air Park, with flights expected to begin within weeks. This initiative aims to reduce delivery costs and emissions, contrasting with other companies exploring long-range deliveries.

title: Walmart US CEO: one-third of stores get a failing grade. Ouch.
summary: Walmart CEO Doug McMillon is defending the company's brick-and-mortar stores as a weapon against Amazon, despite a recent stock dive and sales/profit warnings. The company plans to invest billions into e-commerce to better integrate it with its physical stores. However, the CEO of Walmart U.S. stated that only two-thirds of the stores are currently passing grades for cleanliness and service, indicating a significant need for improvement before the stores can truly be an advantage.

title: Wal-Mart puts the squeeze on suppliers to share its pain as earnings sag
summary: Wal-Mart is intensifying pressure on its suppliers for price cuts and cost sharing after a shock earnings warning, as the retailer faces rising labor costs, store improvement expenses, and investments in online sales. Suppliers are bracing for increased demands, including new fees and extended payment terms, to help Wal-Mart offset its declining profits and maintain competitive pricing against rivals like Amazon.com Inc. Despite initial resistance, most suppliers are expected to comply due to Wal-Mart's significant market power, though some express concerns about a "slippery slope" of continuous demands.

title: GM Just Delivered Some Great News for Detroit
summary: General Motors announced it will nearly double the workforce at its Detroit-Hamtramck Assembly plant by early next year, adding over 1,200 new jobs. This expansion is to meet the forecasted demand for five cars produced at the plant and will increase the total jobs to around 2,800. This news follows a recent similar announcement from Amazon regarding its Detroit operations.

title: GE is using drones to inspect the power grid
summary: General Electric is exploring the use of drones to inspect power grids, aiming to reduce the cost, time, and danger associated with manual inspections. These drones, utilizing software from Airware and built on Amazon Web Services, capture images to identify potential issues like overgrown vegetation and wirelessly transmit data for analysis. While the market for such services is currently niche, Navigant Research predicts significant growth, with revenue expected to skyrocket to $4.1 billion by 2024.

title: Nasdaq may see record with Apple earnings
summary: The Nasdaq 100 index, heavily influenced by US technology stocks such as Apple, is poised to potentially set a new record high, driven by strong earnings anticipated from Apple Inc. Technology shares have led the market's recovery, with gains in Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft following better-than-expected earnings. Despite being an "underperformer" among tech giants recently, Apple's expected revenue increase and positive market sentiment suggest its upcoming earnings report could push the Nasdaq 100 to a record.

title: Review: Should you buy Roku’s new media streaming box?
summary: This article reviews the Roku 4 streaming box, highlighting its new features like 4K streaming, the remote finding feature, and Roku OS7 with enhanced search. The reviewer notes that while it's an excellent device, it's not a significant upgrade from the Roku 3 unless 4K capability is crucial. The article compares it to competitors like Apple TV and Amazon Fire TV, concluding that it's a strong contender for those considering a new streaming box other than the latest Apple TV.

title: Macroeconomic Factors Affecting Microsoft’s Performance
summary: This article discusses the macroeconomic factors affecting Microsoft's performance, primarily focusing on competition in the technology sector and the company's strategic focus on cloud business. It highlights Microsoft's major competitors in the cloud segment, including Amazon, IBM, and Google, and outlines Microsoft's strategy to succeed in the mobile-first and cloud-first space, detailing the resources and focus areas required for growth. The article also provides financial details, noting Microsoft's revenue increase in 1Q16 and its representation in key tech ETFs.

title: Bye-bye HP, Hello HP Enterprise and HP Inc.
summary: On Sunday, Hewlett-Packard will split into two publicly traded companies: Hewlett Packard Enterprise and HP Inc. This move follows a history of strategic missteps and controversial acquisitions for the tech giant, which started in 1939. The split aims to create more focused businesses, with Hewlett Packard Enterprise handling servers, software, storage, networking, and services, while HP Inc. will focus on printers and PCs.

title: VA pushes to top of U.S. data center market
summary: Northern Virginia has become the leading data center market in the U.S., surpassing the New York-New Jersey region with 20% market share. This growth is attributed to lower electricity rates, minimal natural disaster risk, and a strong fiber network. Amazon Web Services is significantly contributing to this trend with the construction of a large solar farm to power its cloud computing data centers in the region.

title: Personal Finance
summary: This extensive resource from NerdWallet covers a wide array of personal finance topics, including credit cards, banking, home loans, personal loans, insurance, investing, small business finance, and taxes. It offers guides, calculators, and advice on managing money, building credit, making money, and paying off debt, alongside current financial news and FAQs. The content is designed to help individuals make informed financial decisions.

title: No More 'Daily Deals': Amazon Is Shutting Down Amazon Local
summary: Amazon.com announced it would discontinue its "daily deals" platform, Amazon Local, starting December 18. This decision follows struggles faced by other daily deals sites like LivingSocial and Groupon, which have both announced significant layoffs recently. Customers will still be able to use vouchers purchased before the December deadline.
